assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.2 [3313,3591) defines the notice-listed passages. [7003,8015) expressly adds media commonly carrying printed covers and specifies legibility, placement and overflow.

challenge.method: Applied the clause to 100 printed copies, 101 copies on qualifying media, and 101 Opaque copies with no Cover Texts required. Tested whether overflow allows the publisher to omit the remaining passages.
challenge.results: Exactly 100 does not trigger either quantity paragraph. At 101, either qualifying medium can trigger the cover requirement when the notice requires texts. Overflow permits continuation in listed order. With 101 Opaque copies and no required Cover Texts, publication or distribution still triggers the independent per-copy Transparent accompaniment or public network-location route.

limitations: The work notice identifies the passages. Whether a medium commonly has printed covers is factual. Publisher identification and front-cover title presentation are additional duties in the paragraph.
reasoning: GNU 1.2 §3 covers both printed copies and copies in media that commonly have printed covers. Publication must exceed 100 qualifying copies and the work’s notice must require Cover Texts. Required passages go legibly on their designated sides. If space is insufficient on either side, the publisher should keep the first listed passages that reasonably fit there and continue the rest on adjacent pages.
